TXG.company_description: Life-sciences tools company selling single-cell (Chromium) and spatial-genomics (Xenium/Visium, new Atera) platforms plus consumables to research and translational labs.

SNPS.company_description: Synopsys develops EDA software and IP for chip design; also provides simulation/analysis tools (post-Ansys acquisition); sells to semiconductor and systems companies; software/semiconductor tools sector.

[2026-05-29] LITE closed at ~$860, down ~18% from the May 11 peak; FN (Fabrinet) -10.6% over the 5d window confirms sector-wide rotation, not an idiosyncratic Lumentum catalyst.

bullets: [2026-05-20] Reported record May client assets of $1.87tn (+22% YoY, +6% sequentially) on higher equity markets and net inflows; PCG fee-based assets +28% YoY, a positive monthly data point reinforcing organic-growth momentum.

SNDK.company_description: SanDisk is a pure-play NAND flash memory and SSD maker (re-spun from Western Digital in 2025), earning revenue selling storage chips into datacenters, PCs and devices via its Kioxia JV.

[2026-05-23] Sell-side framing the AI memory supercycle as fully mainstream (Motley Fool, 24/7 Wall St 'memory melt-up' pieces), with SanDisk a top-performing S&P 500 name in 2026.
[2026-05] AI datacenters estimated to consume ~70% of memory-chip supply this year, keeping NAND tight and pricing elevated into 2027.

GTM.company_description: ZoomInfo (ticker rebranded ZI->GTM in 2025), a B2B go-to-market intelligence platform selling sales/marketing contact data and engagement tools to revenue teams.
bullets: [2026-06-02] Q1 results landed with a sharp cut to full-year 2026 revenue guidance plus a ~20% workforce reduction; stock plunged roughly a third as the print reset the demand narrative.

[2026-06-02] Management/analysts flagged two-plus years of weak client demand and AI-driven shifts in customer behavior eroding the core data-vendor business — an idiosyncratic structural worry, not just multiple compression.

[2026-05-28] Mizuho raised its price target to $115 from $110 (Outperform) on the agentic-trading opportunity.

[2026-05] Secured final Canadian regulatory approval for its WonderFi crypto acquisition, clearing the deal to close and advancing international expansion.

DDOG.company_description: Datadog, a cloud observability and monitoring SaaS platform (infrastructure, APM, logs, security) increasingly positioned as an AI-agent/AI-app monitoring play.

[2026-05] Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank and UBS raised price targets tied to AI ad performance; Q1 2026 revenue +24% to $1.84bn with Q2 guide $1.92-1.95bn.

bullets: [2026-06-03] Broadcom's soft AI guidance triggered a broad semis selloff that dragged down semicap equipment names alongside chipmakers on day two.

bullets: [2026-06-02] At Computex, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang appeared on stage with CEO Matt Murphy and called Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company,' its networking chips 'essential' to AI data centers, sparking a single-session jump above +32%.

[2026-06-02] Move was idiosyncratic — AVGO -13.8%, ARM -15.3%, NVDA -6.9% over the same window — driven by Marvell-specific custom-silicon endorsement and S&P 500 inclusion, not a sector tide.

[2026-06-05] Modest gain alongside US network/low-cost airlines (ALK +2.0%, LUV +0.9%), consistent with a benign sector tape.

bullets: [2026-06-04] Visa and Mastercard reported to be backing a new stablecoin platform alongside Stripe (Coinbase exploring participation), supporting the payment-networks crypto-rails narrative.

bullets: [2026-06-03] Mastercard announced expanded settlement to include stablecoins (USDC, PYUSD, RLUSD, etc.) plus intraday, weekend and holiday settlement across chains like Base, Solana and Polygon — a positive crypto-rails narrative that lifted shares.

[2026-04] Q1 2026 net revenue +15.8% and adjusted EPS +23.3% YoY, beating consensus for a 20th straight quarter — a strong fundamental backdrop.

2344.TW.company_description: Winbond Electronics is a Taiwanese maker of specialty/niche DRAM and NOR/flash memory, a smaller-cap memory name leveraged to the broader DRAM cycle.
bullets: [2026-06-03] Broadcom's disappointing AI-chip outlook ignited a two-day global semiconductor selloff that swept up the entire memory complex including Taiwanese DRAM names.
[2026-06-05] As a higher-beta, smaller-cap memory proxy, Winbond fell more than larger peers in the de-risking, mirroring SK Hynix (-9.92%) and Nanya 2408.TW (-8.86%).
[2026-06-05] No Winbond-specific news surfaced; the decline reflects sector-wide AI-bubble anxiety and unwinding of the memory supercycle trade rather than a company catalyst.

000660.KS.company_description: SK Hynix is the world's leading HBM supplier and second-largest DRAM/NAND maker, the prime memory beneficiary of AI accelerator demand (key Nvidia HBM partner).
bullets: [2026-06-02] Stock hit an all-time high (~KRW 2,407,000) capping a strong AI-memory run, leaving it set up for a sharp momentum reversal over the week.

bullets: [2026-06-05] Strong May jobs report pushed Treasury yields up (10y ~4.54%) and damped Fed-cut odds; higher-for-longer rates lift cash-sweep net interest income for advisor platforms, the dominant driver of the wealth-manager rally over the week.

BESI.AS.company_description: Besi (BE Semiconductor Industries) is a Dutch maker of chip assembly equipment — die-attach, packaging and the leading hybrid-bonding tools used for advanced AI/HBM stacking.
bullets: [2026-06-04] Broadcom guided Q3 AI chip revenue to ~$16bn vs ~$17.2bn consensus and declined to raise its FY26 AI forecast; shares fell ~13-14% after the print, triggering a sector-wide AI 'sell-the-news' reset.

[2026-06-05] Besi diverged because its hybrid-bonding/advanced-packaging franchise is tied to HBM4 and AI chiplet stacking rather than the WFE/memory-capacity cycle hitting US names — the same structural story behind Q1 orders up ~104% YoY to €269.7m.

[2026-06-05] European equipment names held or rose as a regional rotation away from the US-listed AI complex (ASML +1.1%, ASM.AS +0.2%); Besi's lithography-adjacent, packaging-led demand was seen as insulated from the Broadcom/memory read-through.

bullets: [2026-06-03] Earnings aftermath kept weighing: a wider-than-expected ~$740M Q1 net loss and soft Q2 revenue guidance, with massive ~$7.7B capex and deeply negative free cash flow, reset the premium valuation.
